proves: launch threshold "zero unrelated evidence surfaces in a named-subject answer"
question: What's the status of meridian/web-app?

invariants.assert: When a question names a specific subject (a single repository/project/team), every fact, metric, evidence ref, and change item in the answer must be scoped to that named subject -- evidence belonging to any other repository/project the org happens to also have (meridian/atlas, meridian/api-gateway, meridian/context-fabric, legacy/billing, etc.) must never leak into a named-subject answer, ranked or unranked, cited or uncited. This is a launch-blocking threshold, not a nice-to-have: a named-subject answer that quietly blends in unrelated org evidence is indistinguishable, from the caller's perspective, from a correct answer, which makes the failure mode invisible without this explicit check.
invariants.$comment: check=no_internal_error is a real, always-meaningful floor (the run must not crash to internal_error) but is NARROWER than this invariant's full 'assert' claim above -- Lane 2a's invariants.py registry (read directly, 2026-08-06) has no checker yet for the specific widening/unauthorized-candidate/persistence claim this category names. Tracked as a Lane 2a checker gap, not silently claimed as fully enforced.

notes: Question text matches provider-scripts/role-legacy_agent.json's `cases["unrelated-evidence.named-subject"].question` verbatim (kind: delegate_default -- falls through to the pre-existing default heuristic, `_evidence_query_from_question`'s named-repository literal derivation, unchanged; this case exists to make that question individually addressable in the fault/conformance matrix, per the file's own doc comment). The 'unrelated evidence' being guarded against is real in this fixture world: subjects.json/world.json realize several OTHER primary-org repositories/projects alongside meridian/web-app (meridian/atlas, meridian-sandbox/atlas, meridian/api-gateway, meridian/context-fabric, legacy/billing) -- a close-match or evidence-aggregation bug that fails to scope tool results to the resolved subject would have real unrelated rows available to leak, not a hypothetical. Distinct from `subject-label.wrong-kind-collision` (CHAOS-3422: a project mention losing to unrelated work-item/PR-title substring hits within its OWN correct evidence set) -- this case is about evidence from a DIFFERENT repository/project entirely.
$comment_resolution_path_invariant: resolution_path_in REMOVED (CHAOS-3462 B4). This case's question names ZERO mentions that production's extract_mentions recognizes -- verified by executing the REAL producer -- QuestionInterpreter.interpret plus SubjectPreflight.run with this runner's exact request shape -- against this question text. NOTE (adversarial round 2): an earlier version of this comment cited extract_mentions, which is the WRONG oracle: production additionally mints untyped bare-name mentions via _add_untyped_mentions, and three cases were mis-dispositioned on that basis. This case's zero-mention conclusion was re-confirmed against the real interpreter. CASE-SCHEMA.v1.md's own 'practical extraction gotcha' is the cause: a bare, unquoted, lowercase slug is not a mention. So no dev_run_resolutions row is ever written, derive_resolution_path returns None BY CONTRACT, and resolution_path_in deliberately never matches None -- the check failed by construction on every run, on every stack. Same trap and same disposition as the four scope_resolution_outcome_in cases in CASE-SCHEMA.v1.md S1: drop the unpassable check, keep the narrower floor the remaining invariants give, and say so out loud rather than claim enforcement this case never had. The profile's null resolution_path is CORRECT and stays.
